name: Moana Surfrider, a Westin Resort
insider_take: Known as the "First Lady of Waikiki," this legendary beachfront resort has been the crown jewel of Hawaiian hospitality since 1901, blending timeless elegance with authentic island charm.
whats_special: The Moana Surfrider is Hawaii's oldest hotel and sits on the exact spot where Hawaiian royalty once relaxed. Its iconic Banyan Tree, planted in 1904, has become one of Waikiki's most photographed landmarks. The resort's Victorian architecture creates a stunning contrast against Diamond Head's volcanic silhouette, while its prime Waikiki Beach location offers some of the most consistent surf breaks on the island.
pro_tip: Book a table at the Banyan Tree for afternoon tea – it's positioned perfectly under the historic banyan tree where you can watch surfers while enjoying Hawaiian-inspired pastries and listening to live traditional music.
dont_miss: The nightly torch lighting ceremony at sunset, followed by cocktails at the Beachhouse at the Moana while watching world-class surfers ride the famous waves just steps from your table. The hotel's museum on the second floor showcases fascinating artifacts from Waikiki's royal past.
pros: Historic beachfront property known as 'First Lady of Waikiki'
Prime location directly on Waikiki Beach with stunning ocean views
Elegant Victorian architecture and timeless Hawaiian hospitality
Multiple dining options including beachfront restaurants and lounges
cons: Historic building may have smaller room sizes compared to newer resorts
Premium pricing due to prime beachfront location and historic significance
